title: Taskify maintenance checklists into reactive microflows
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:
We currently maintain a large set of manual maintenance checklists used by SRE and Support for routine operations (e.g., tenant quota resets, cache warmups, instance switchover, model rollback). These checklists are long, freeform, and often invoked during incidents or scheduled maintenance. They are error-prone and difficult to audit.

Goal:
Convert high-frequency maintenance checklists into 'reactive microflows' — compact, typed task chains that can be executed as atomic, idempotent operations from the Console or CLI. Each microflow should:
- accept structured inputs (typed parameters)
- validate preconditions and RBAC before running
- support dry-run/simulate mode and a sandboxed replay environment
- emit structured telemetry (event start/step results/finish) to the Ops pipeline
- be composable (call other microflows) and versioned

Scope for this ticket:
- Prototype a reference microflow for "quota-reset-and-notify" and one for "model-variant-fallback" that demonstrates precondition checks, preflight dry-run, and telemetry hooks.
- Build a minimal microflow runner service (stateless, serverless-friendly) + a Console action that calls the runner with typed inputs.
- Add safe gating: canary mode (SRE-only), permission gating (RBAC), and a kill-switch for automated runs.

Design notes / Architecture overview:
1) Microflow model: YAML-first manifests with typed inputs, step definitions (shell/GH actions/console-api calls), expected success conditions, and compensation steps. Keep manifest small so it can be rendered in the Console inline.
2) Runner: Golang service exposing a POST /run-microflow that validates manifest, resolves secrets via KMS proxy, executes steps in sequence with retries/backoff, records step outputs to the event stream, and supports --dry-run.
3) Safety: built-in idempotency tokens, step-level timeouts, and automatic revert on failure using compensation steps.
4) Telemetry: span per microflow and per-step, push structured events to the ops-telemetry kafka topic, and surface a quick trace link in Console.
5) Storage: manifests stored in runbook-catalog (existing DB table), versions tracked by manifest hash.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- We could implement runner as a Lua sandbox to support faster step execution, but chosen Golang runner gives clearer process isolation and easier integration with existing infra.
- Manifests are YAML to be human-editable; we will validate into a typed proto before execution to avoid runaway scripts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype runner can execute the two reference microflows end-to-end in dry-run and real-run modes.
- Console integration button that opens typed input form and shows dry-run output.
- Telemetry events for start/step/end appear in ops-telemetry and linkable from Console.
- RBAC gating prevents non-privileged users from running sensitive microflows.
- Documentation + runbook entry in Confluence and a sample GitHub PR for the manifests.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: prototype runner + manifests (alpha) for SRE team only.
- Week 2: feedback loop, add step-level compensation and expand telemetry.
- Week 3: invite first-tier Support to beta; enable guarded Console button behind feature flag.
- Week 4: wider rollout and retro to decide which checklists to fully migrate.

Integration links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Microflow+Design+Draft
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-microflows/pull/42
- Telemetry dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/microflow-runs

Notes on metrics to watch:
- Mean time to complete a microflow (dry-run vs live)
- Fraction of runs that trigger compensation steps
- Reduction in manual checklist edits after migration

Security review notes:
- Must pass secrets exposure audit; runner will never accept inline secrets — only KMS-referenced tokens.
- Every microflow with elevated permissions must have an SRE owner and a documented rationale.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Two reference microflows (quota-reset-and-notify, model-variant-fallback) run successfully in alpha with telemetry. 2) Console flow supports typed inputs and dry-run. 3) RBAC enforces access restrictions; unauthorized attempts are logged. 4) Documentation and example manifests merged to ops-microflows repo.
design_notes: See 'Architecture overview' in description. Key implementation details: use protobuf validation for typed inputs, instrument each runner call with trace.id, and persist run metadata for audit. Avoid allowing arbitrary shell steps in manifests without explicit SRE review; prefer bounded API step primitives (call-console-api, gh-pr-comment, kms-get-secret, infra-api).
test_plan: Unit tests for runner step execution, integration test using local kafka mock for telemetry, end-to-end smoke that runs the prototype manifests in a staging tenant. Add a simulated failure run to verify compensation paths. Include a dry-run acceptance test in CI that runs at PR time.
